spec_reference: gh-audit-ruflo.md §24 HARD ADOPTION BLOCKERS (lines 1178-1204). Blocker wording below is quoted from that list verbatim.
scope_key: whole product = the blocker holds on the default install path with no opt-in. specific capability = the blocker condemns one named capability, not the product. opt-in surface only = the blocker holds only where an explicitly enabled, non-default surface is used.

hard_blockers.blocker: a successful response without a durable postcondition
hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-011: `ruflo verify` prints 'pass: 0, drift: 53, regressed: 0, missing: 2' then '[OK] All fixes verified' and exits 0 on a pristine install (work/verify-npm.txt; dist/src/commands/verify.js:201,244). RUF-401: memory store prints '[OK] Data stored successfully', exits 0, and discards the write — DB byte-identical, sentinel absent from a full-filesystem grep (evidence/test-results.json#S02-S06,S16). RUF-402: verifyMemoryInit reports 'Verification passed (6/6 tests)' in exactly that state (#S07). RUF-440: 6 concurrent `issues claim` callers all print '[OK] Claimed' and exit 0 while 2-3 claims are discarded, 3/3 trials (work/lane-L4b/logs/t14-claimlost.log). RUF-201: memory_store returns stored:true and a second process reads totalEntries:0 (evidence/full-init-process-diff.json). RUF-300: `plugins list` prints 'Registry discovered: 21 plugins available' with a random CID after all five gateways fail, exit 0 (work/lane-L3b/logs/net-sink/plugins.out). RUF-L6b-03: github_pr_manage returns {success:true, action:'merged'} from a local JSON store when `gh` is absent (github-tools.js:333-337). RUF-002: init prints 'Files: 111 created' having created 255.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: This is the audit's defining defect class. It reproduces independently in provenance verification, memory persistence, ownership claiming, plugin discovery, GitHub actions and init self-reporting — six unrelated subsystems on the default path. It is not confined to one capability and is not opt-in.
hard_blockers.spike_corroboration: Strengthened by spike evidence merged after the initial synthesis pass.

hard_blockers.blocker: direct Ruflo mutation of the company repository
hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-208: starting the MCP server alone, with no init, writes 9 artifacts into the repository including ruvector.db (1,589,248 B) at the root (evidence/full-init-process-diff.json#mcp_execution_surface). RUF-411: every `memory` subcommand — including read-only ones — spawns a 7-worker daemon and writes 6 repository files plus one HOME file (evidence/test-results.json#S18). RUF-L6a-04: 32 distinct repo-local state path literals across 219 process.cwd() sites; even agent_execute writes .claude-flow/agents/store.json (agent-execute-core.js:31-34,405). RUF-009: init modifies the tracked .gitignore and writes a binary into the repository root. RUF-314: .swarm/, ruvector.db, .mcp.json and 241 .claude/ files are not gitignored.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: There is no read-only mode. Compatibility question Q5 answers NO. The only containment is to point Ruflo at a directory that is not the company repository, which is a deployment constraint rather than a product capability.
hard_blockers.spike_corroboration: Strengthened by spike evidence merged after the initial synthesis pass.

hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-011: the Ed25519 seed is sha256(gitCommit + ':ruflo-witness/v1') — both inputs public, so the private key is publicly derivable and any party can forge a valid signature (verify.js:124). RUF-012: the manifest is fetched at runtime from the mutable branch fix/issues-may-1-3 (verify.js:21,139,161), so what 'verified' means can change at any time, and the verification/ directory ships in neither tarball. RUF-L2a-004: src/ is not shipped, dist is git-ignored (.gitignore:104), neither tarball ships a LICENSE, and the one comparable checked-in artifact diverges (helpers.manifest.json 3.34.0 with one signature in source vs 3.37.0 with a different signature in the tarball). RUF-304@AUD-L3a: all three bundleDependencies return E404 at their pinned versions while 372 files of their code ship inside the tarball. RUF-L2a-009: proven-config.signed.rvf asserts benchmark receipts against a corpus present in neither tarball.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: Verification fails from both directions: the vendor's own verify command produces no integrity evidence, and independent verification of the artifact against the tagged source is not possible either.

hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-003: `ruflo init` with no global flag appends a 'Ruflo Integration' block to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and creates ~/.claude-flow/update-state.json; the appended block instructs any Claude Code agent to invoke ruflo MCP tools (work/global-overwrite/). RUF-205: the global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md is NOT restored by cleanup --force (46 to 369 B). RUF-213/RUF-316: every hook falls back to $HOME/.claude/helpers/, so a partially-cleaned repository executes the user's global copy.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: The write is APPEND-ONLY and non-destructive, and the pre-existing global settings.json and CLAUDE.md content survive verbatim (RUF-003, VERIFIED) — but it is unrequested, machine-wide, has no opt-in flag, and is not reverted by the uninstall path. RUFLO_NO_SKILLS_SH / --no-skills-sh do not cover it.

hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-202: `ruflo cleanup` — including the documented DRY RUN — starts a background daemon and never stops it; the daemon survives cleanup --force (ps -ef, PPID 1). RUF-505: `ruflo status`, `memory list` and even `memory --help` spawn a --quiet daemon with 7 periodic workers and a 12 h TTL, measured at 4.20 CPU-seconds over 418 s, ~100 MB RSS. RUF-211 and RUF-L6a-03: SessionStart spawns detached, unref'd children explicitly designed to outlive the hook; grandchildren reparent to init and escape Tailered's direct-child-only kill (TAI-002, a PRE-EXISTING TAILERED FINDING).
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: The daemon itself stops cleanly when asked and opens no listening sockets (RUF-221, positive). The blocker is that it starts without consent from read-only commands and from the uninstaller, and that detached grandchildren outlive every kill path the host has.

hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-440: 2-3 of 6 concurrent claims silently discarded, 3/3 trials, with proven overlapping ownership. RUF-441: root cause is an unlocked read-modify-write persisted by non-atomic whole-file fs.writeFileSync (claim-service.ts:258,265-286) while the correct locked/atomic pattern exists unused in workspace-lease.ts:92-142. RUF-444: daemon mutual exclusion is PID-based and two live daemons ran on one shared repository across PID namespaces (host-verified via docker top). RUF-L1b-07: 'Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus' is unlocked vote arithmetic over one JSON file.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: Scoped deliberately. The STORAGE layer is sound — cross-project isolation holds, concurrent distinct-key writes are never lost, and integrity_check passes after contention, SIGABRT and SIGKILL (RUF-455, positive). The corruption is in the OWNERSHIP and COORDINATION layer: claims, hive-mind consensus, and cross-namespace daemon exclusion.

hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-446: memory_entries.owner_id is declared and indexed but never written by any INSERT or UPDATE; provenance_type is always 'unknown' despite ADR-323's enum; expires_at is always NULL, verified across every database produced in the lane. RUF-206: repoHash — the ledger key — changes from one memory_store touching no company file. RUF-416: the metadata table records the wrong storage backend.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: Scoped to Ruflo's own state: nothing Ruflo writes can be attributed to a run or an agent. It does not by itself break causal links that Tailered maintains outside Ruflo.

hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-417: `workflow run` exits 0, writes a status:'running' checkpoint, executes nothing, and never writes a terminal state (evidence/test-results.json#S22,S25). RUF-418: `workflow list` can never list anything, so the zombie records are also invisible. RUF-409: autopilot treats an unreadable task source as 'no tasks' and reports ALLOW STOP at 0/0 (100%).
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: Scoped to the workflow and autopilot subsystems. Autopilot CHECKPOINTS are durable across processes and real terminal states do exist for max-iterations and disabled (AUD-L4 passing capabilities); the failure is on the `workflow run` path and in fail-open completion.

hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-L6a-12: provider failures are returned as SUCCESSFUL tool results carrying {success:false, error} (agent-execute-core.js:100-104,142,165), so an adapter reading the transport layer records a failed model call as completed. RUF-404: `memory init` reports failure AFTER its work committed — a false failure. RUF-301@AUD-L3b: init aborts with SIGABRT after writing 250 files, with no completion signal and a non-zero exit.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: Scoped to the agent-execution and memory-init surfaces. Correctable in an adapter that inspects the payload rather than the transport status, which is why it is not product-wide.

hard_blockers.blocker: executed provider or model differing from the authorized selection
hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-304@AUD-L3b: provider is chosen by ambient environment (agent-execute-core.js:71-106) — no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY plus OPENROUTER_API_KEY routes to openrouter.ai, plus OLLAMA_API_KEY routes to ollama.com — and the success shape AnthropicCallResult has no provider or endpoint field by explicit design. RUF-L6a-01: determineAgentModel (agent-tools.js:127-131) silently discards any model outside five literals; agent_execute accepts no model at all. RUF-305@AUD-L3b: agent-execute-core.js:111 hardcodes https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages, bypassing ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. RUF-312@AUD-L3b: init writes "model": "claude-sonnet-5" into the host project's settings.json unasked.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: Scoped to the agent_execute / agent_spawn capability and to init's harness-configuration write. This is the DEFAULT-path instance of the model-identity blocker and is separate from RUF-010 below. Live fallback ordering under real credentials is UNKNOWN — no credentials existed in the containers.

hard_blockers.blocker: executed provider or model differing from the authorized selection
hard_blockers.evidence: Upstream's own v3.37.0 release notes disclose that the cloud plane 'picks a tier per prompt instead of honoring the client's requested model' (upstream/release-v3.37.0.json). v3.37.0 adds --routing-mode <auto|low|mid|high> to pin a TIER; pinning a tier is not pinning a MODEL.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: EXPLICITLY SCOPED, do not inflate. This applies to the `ruflo proxy` surface when the cloud plane is enabled. The meta-proxy is not installed by `npm i` or by `init`, cloud routing defaults to 'passthrough', and the consent framework defaults every domain to granted:false (RUF-325, VERIFIED positive). It is NOT evidence that a default Ruflo install substitutes models; that was not observed. It blocks adoption of the proxy/cloud-routing capability specifically and requires any integration to disable it explicitly rather than rely on defaults. Note that RUF-210 shows the default-on UserPromptSubmit hook advertises this opt-in surface inside the agent's context.

hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-406: headless-worker-executor.js contains ZERO policy-engine references; cost is parsed post-hoc from the result envelope (line 371); the only gated surface never supplies costUsd. RUF-L6a-02: no Ruflo surface returns a hard pre-execution {maxCostUsd, maxTokens}. RUF-407: the ledger accumulates IEEE-754 float USD (4.000000000000002 from 40 x $0.10). RUF-408: `policy budget set` refuses in any non-TTY context, so the only cost control is unconfigurable from CI, containers or headless sessions. RUF-L6a-08: Ruflo's own measured $1.56/call x >=4 calls = $6.24 against a $5.00 exclusive cap.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: No configuration achieves a hard pre-spend ceiling. The policy budget check that DOES exist is genuine, pre-decision, persistent across processes and hash-chained (AUD-L4 passing capabilities) — but it is not on the model-spending path and cannot be configured in automation. Success of `policy budget set` under a genuine pty is UNKNOWN.
hard_blockers.spike_corroboration: Strengthened by spike evidence merged after the initial synthesis pass.

hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-305@AUD-L3b: two Anthropic call sites in the same package disagree — managed-agent-tools.js:20 honours ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, agent-execute-core.js:111 is a bare literal. RUF-L6a-01: Ruflo ships a stateful Thompson-bandit router persisting .swarm/model-router-state.json and preempts the caller's model on retryable errors (agent-execute-core.js:425-456, FALLBACK_MAX_RETRIES=1 at :423), which answers compatibility question Q11 NO.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: Scoped to the agent-execution path. It is the same mechanism as the model-identity blocker viewed from the routing side; a gateway-routed environment such as the agent platform's is bypassed on that path only.

hard_blockers.blocker: inability to stop or remove Ruflo
hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-205: cleanup --force reverts 56 of 258 changes (21.7%); 204 files, 57 directories, ruvector.db, .mcp.json, CLAUDE.md, the .gitignore edit and the global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md block all survive. RUF-202: cleanup starts a daemon it never stops. RUF-209: the surviving settings.json keeps the permission grants, the model pin and a statusLine pointing at deleted helpers whose $HOME fallback then executes the user's global copy. RUF-212: the mutable-tag .mcp.json survives. RUF-447: per-agent branches are never deleted.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: Removal by discarding a disposable worktree DOES work, and the Tailered repository still validates in all three states (RUF-222, positive) — but the vendor's own uninstall path does not remove Ruflo, and it cannot remove the global and out-of-repository state at all.

hard_blockers.blocker: autonomous modification of policy or accepted decisions
hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-309: plain `init` injects permissions.allow ['Bash(npx @claude-flow*)','Bash(npx claude-flow*)','Bash(node .claude/*)','mcp__claude-flow__*'] into an existing settings.json without prompting — a standing grant to execute any of the 241 files it just wrote under .claude/ — and sets CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 (work/lane-L3b/logs/ctl4.log). RUF-303@AUD-L3b: `init --force` replaces project settings.json and .mcp.json WHOLESALE; 0 of 6 configuration canaries survived. RUF-312@AUD-L3b: init pins the harness model. RUF-L6b-09: the .claude/ tree it grants itself execution over contains auto-commit.sh with AUTO_PUSH=true by default.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: A tool writing its own execution allowlist into the host's security policy is a privilege escalation by construction. Both the merging (plain init) and replacing (--force) paths trigger it, so it is not avoidable by flag choice.

hard_blockers.blocker: inability to preserve the founder gate
hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-L6b-01: github_pr_manage action merge runs `gh pr merge <N> --merge` with no CI-status, approval or branch-protection precondition (github-tools.js:322), auto-approved by the mcp__claude-flow__* grant init adds. RUF-L6b-02: github_workflow runs `gh workflow run <id> --ref <ref>` (:565) and `gh run cancel` (:574), reaching manually-gated CI workflows and able to cancel the gates that would catch the result. RUF-L6b-09: auto-commit.sh defaults AUTO_PUSH=true.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED (packaged code and permission grant) / INFERRED (the agent platform deploy consequence)
hard_blockers.scope_note: Scoped to the GitHub tool family. The packaged code and the auto-approving permission grant are VERIFIED; that a merge constitutes a production deploy is a property of the the agent platform host (CLAUDE.md:291) and the end-to-end consequence was not executed, so it is INFERRED. For the agent platform specifically this is the decisive blocker on any write-capable adoption.

hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-301@AUD-L3a: `ruflo` declares MIT while 499 of 526 files (94.87%) are a fork of Apache-2.0 huggingface/chat-ui v0.20.0. RUF-302@AUD-L3a: neither tarball ships a LICENSE, so both fail the MIT notice condition for their own grant. RUF-303@AUD-L3a: zero NOTICE files anywhere and 0 of 358 files in the vendored subtree carry a copyright header or modification notice, against Apache-2.0 4(b)/(c). RUF-306@AUD-L3a: 24 HuggingChat trademarked brand assets ship verbatim, including a manifest.json declaring name 'HuggingChat', while Apache-2.0 section 6 grants no trademark rights.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: SCOPED TO THE `ruflo` WRAPPER PACKAGE, which is where the vendored subtree lives. Depending on `@claude-flow/cli` directly removes the entire 499-file Apache-2.0 payload and the trademarked assets. Zero GPL and zero AGPL appear anywhere in the closure (RUF-315@AUD-L3a, positive). These are technical license observations, not legal advice, and the clearance is bounded to the upstream development lockfile (stale at 3.35.0).

hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-306@AUD-L3b: refreshRemoteMessages() fetches https://funnel.ruv.io/v1/messages with NO consent gate anywhere in its path, is spawned detached from the SessionStart hook init installs, and renders unsigned content in the developer's statusline; doctor states 'Funnel (ADR-305): enabled (decided by: package-default; disclosure: never_seen)'. RUF-320@AUD-L3b: one `plugins list` produced 21 requests to api.npmjs.org plus one to a vendor Cloud Function whose actions include track-download and analytics, with no consent domain gating it. RUF-004/RUF-313@AUD-L3b: init downloads a 90,387,606-byte ONNX model, undeclared in any lockfile and with no integrity check, into node_modules. RUF-012: `ruflo verify` fetches its trust anchor from raw.githubusercontent.com at verify time.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: The consent framework itself is correctly built and defaults to granted:false for all twelve domains (RUF-325, positive); the /v1/events telemetry path DOES gate on it. The blocker is that /v1/messages, the npm registry calls and the Cloud Function call bypass the framework rather than break it, and all fire on the default install path.

hard_blockers.blocker: sensitive prompt, source, or credential leakage
hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-314@AUD-L3b: .swarm/agentdb-memory.db is mode 0644 (world-readable) beside a 0600 memory.db; a stored value was recovered verbatim with `strings`; doctor states 'Encryption at Rest: Off'; and .swarm/, ruvector.db, .mcp.json and 241 .claude/ files are NOT gitignored, so `git add -A` stages them. RUF-308@AUD-L3b: `memory export --output ../../../tmp/…` wrote outside the project root — an arbitrary-file-write primitive. RUF-445: `memory search` and `memory list` default to ALL namespaces and returned another namespace's secret to an unscoped caller.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: Scoped to the memory subsystem and to data deliberately stored in it. AMBIENT credentials did NOT leak: with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and DB-URL canaries in the environment, neither appeared in any Ruflo artifact after doctor, status and memory store (RUF-326, VERIFIED negative). The exposure is of what an agent puts into memory, plus the export path.

hard_blockers.blocker: Ruflo becoming a second canonical ledger
hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-203: after `ruflo init` the Tailered context snapshot admits 96 files of which ZERO are Tailered governing files — 100% eviction of AGENTS.md, 4 ADRs and 13 docs — while `validate` still reports VERIFIED. RUF-206: one memory_store changed repoHash, the ledger key. RUF-L6a-09: .claude-flow/ and .swarm/ fall outside the snapshot's six exclusions. RUF-009: 14 mutable SQLite tables plus a 1.5 MB binary enter the repository that ADR-000:19 declares sole company state.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: Recorded as a blocker because Ruflo's state both enters the repository hash and displaces the repository's own governing content, so the two stores compete. Bounded by RUF-222 (positive): the Tailered validator still passes in all three states — which is precisely why the displacement is silent. The three enabling mechanisms are PRE-EXISTING TAILERED design properties, recorded on RUF-203, not Ruflo defects.

hard_blockers.blocker: inability to run within a disposable worker
hard_blockers.evidence: RUF-444: daemon mutual exclusion is PID-based and two live daemons ran on one bind-mounted repository across PID namespaces — the containerised topology is exactly where it fails. RUF-450: agent worktrees are created OUTSIDE the repository at dirname(repoRoot)/.ruflo-worktrees/, escaping the boundary a disposable worktree would define. RUF-L6a-03: detached grandchildren reparent to init and survive the host's kill paths. RUF-403: the SAME install directory persists on glibc and loses every write on musl with no error, so a disposable container's base image silently determines durability.
hard_blockers.label: VERIFIED
hard_blockers.scope_note: Scoped deliberately. Ruflo DOES run inside a disposable container — every execution lane in this audit did exactly that. The blocker is that the isolation properties a disposable worker is supposed to provide (single-instance, boundary containment, kill-on-teardown, environment-independent behaviour) do not hold, so containerisation contains the blast radius without making the behaviour correct.

unresolved_areas.area: Live provider behaviour under real credentials — the actual endpoint contacted, the actual model served, and fallback ordering under 429/5xx
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: No API credentials exist in the audit containers and the charter forbids creating them; paid model calls are forbidden.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: A founder-authorised, USD-capped run against a gateway that logs the executed model and endpoint independently of Ruflo's own reporting. AUD-L5 section 9 contains an executable 10-scenario design (S1-S10) with 7 preconditions, ready to run.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Model-driven performance and cost — task throughput, token efficiency, cost per accepted change, and any comparison against the Tailered baseline on model-dependent axes
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: Paid model calls forbidden. Only model-independent axes (install footprint, CLI/MCP latency, hook overhead, idle/background cost) were measured.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: Execute the AUD-L5 section 9 benchmark under the stated preconditions, reporting 3 repetitions without averaging away non-determinism.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: meta-proxy runtime behaviour — routing, logging, retention, and what api.cognitum.one receives; whether Cognitum retains, logs or trains on routed prompts
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: cognitum-one/meta-proxy source is private; only the signed distribution is public and it was never downloaded or executed. Retention questions require the vendor's live service and terms.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: Vendor terms plus an instrumented run against the proxy with a controlled prompt corpus. Note RUF-324 VERIFIED that the proxy INSTALL path is genuinely hardened; the unknown is the binary's behaviour, not its delivery.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Behaviour behind the `training-data-sharing` and `hosted-memory` consent domains once granted
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: Never granted; granting would produce real egress to vendor infrastructure.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: A sandboxed grant with full egress capture and a synthetic corpus.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Architecture scope of the better-sqlite3 SIGABRT (RUF-301@AUD-L3b, RUF-207, RUF-404, RUF-443, RUF-502)
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: All runs were linux/arm64 on Node v24.19.0. The shared installs' prebuilt .node binaries are ELF aarch64, so an amd64 container cannot exercise the same artifact and cross-arch emulation cannot load them. Node 22 was also untested.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: A native linux/x86_64 host performing its own default install, plus a Node 22 pass. This matters because the whole 'the default install is broken' conclusion may be architecture-specific.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Whether `policy budget set` succeeds under a genuine pty
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: No pty was allocatable from the audit harness (`script` failed with 'tcgetattr/ioctl: Operation not supported on socket'). Refusal in non-TTY and stdout-only-TTY contexts is VERIFIED.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: An interactive terminal session on a developer machine. It would not change RUF-408's automation conclusion, only its interactive one.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Credentialed workflow and autopilot execution — whether a real run writes step-level progress, and whether resume replays completed external effects (the 'duplicate irreversible effects after retry' blocker)
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: No model credentials. Static reading established only that a checkpoint file exists, that autopilot keeps no effect ledger, and that the `workflow run` path writes no terminal state.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: A credentialed run with an externally observable idempotent effect (for example a counter file) and a forced interruption plus resume. This is the one hard blocker in the specification's list that this audit could NOT test.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: hive-mind, swarm and autopilot multi-agent coordination behaviour under concurrency
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: Exercising them requires model calls, which the charter forbids. Their concurrency behaviour is therefore unmeasured, although the underlying consensus implementation was read (RUF-L1b-07).
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: A credentialed multi-agent run with independent observation of who owned what.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: `global-ai-budget` reserve-and-settle correctness under concurrency
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: Read but not exercised; it was budget-lane scope and shares the PID-liveness defect class of RUF-444.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: A concurrency harness against the budget ledger, ideally across PID namespaces given RUF-444.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Whether the mock random-vector embedding fallback (RUF-419) actually degrades semantic search
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: Documented in Ruflo's own shipped source but not reproduced: on every install where that path is reachable, nothing persists at all, so embedding quality is unobservable. Labelled INFERRED.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: An install where the fallback path is reachable AND persistence works, then a semantic-quality probe with known-similar and known-dissimilar pairs.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Whether the invalid published .claude/settings.json (RUF-L1a-01) is ever read at runtime, and whether the postinstall's 12-level upward walk escapes the dependency subtree in a real layout (RUF-L1a-07)
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: Both are REACHABLE questions and the inventory lane's ceiling was PACKAGED. The coordinator executed the postinstall against a SYNTHETIC agentdb tree (RUF-001) but not against a real pnpm monorepo layout.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: Run the postinstall inside a disposable copy of a pnpm monorepo and enumerate every mutated path.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Whether any Ruflo egress path, hook, daemon or MCP tool activates on a the agent platform-shaped install, and whether 3.37.0's hook entries displace or coexist with the agent platform's UserPromptSubmit plus three SessionStart hooks
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: AUD-L6b was read-only by charter; nothing was installed or executed against the agent platform. The 3.36.0 trial preserved the agent platform's hooks byte-identically, but RUF-006 records that hook behaviour changed between 3.36.0 and 3.37.0.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: A 3.37.0 init against a disposable the agent platform clone outside the the agent platform repository, with a full before/after manifest.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: `daemon install-supervisor` (launchd / systemd-user) survival across cleanup, and whether `daemon start --headless` (E2B) or `daemon budget` spend money
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: Installing a supervisor would write outside the audit sandbox on the host; the headless and budget paths need API keys the containers deliberately lack. cleanup's artifact list does not mention any supervisor unit.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: A disposable VM where a host-level supervisor may be installed and then removed.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Whether Claude Code end-to-end treats the exit-1 pre-bash hook as non-blocking (RUF-204)
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: The exit code 1 was observed directly (VERIFIED), but Claude Code was not driven end to end; the conclusion that the command therefore runs rests on documented exit-2 blocking semantics.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: An instrumented Claude Code session with the hook installed and a denylisted command attempted.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Whether the fabricated demo plugin catalog (RUF-300) is ever INSTALLED FROM rather than merely listed, and whether the plugin store enforces the registry checksum before executing plugin code
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: The `plugins install` path was not exercised; doing so would execute third-party plugin code fetched over IPFS.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: A sinkholed `plugins install` against the demo catalog in a throwaway container, observing whether the placeholder checksums (RUF-319) are enforced.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Full functional parity of the `--omit=optional` tree, which is this audit's highest-leverage containment control (RUF-321)
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: Only presence and absence were measured (124 MB / 11,956 files vs 1.5 GB / 50,012). AUD-L4 separately found that on such installs memory persistence is a total no-op (RUF-401), so the mitigation trades one failure class for another.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: A capability matrix run against the reduced tree, command by command, with independent postcondition checks.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Windows and macOS-native behaviour; native-filesystem (non-virtiofs) cold-start figures
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: Only linux/arm64 containers were available, and every measurement ran over Docker Desktop's macOS virtiofs. Cold figures are upper bounds on this host; warm figures are unaffected.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: Runs on native Linux and Windows hosts.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Whether commands that showed zero DNS activity contact hosts under other configurations
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: Absence of observation is scoped to the exact runs recorded — logged out, no consent granted, no proxy installed, warm caches. AUD-L3b labelled this INFERRED rather than VERIFIED.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: Egress capture across the configuration matrix (logged in, consent granted, cold cache, proxy installed).
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: The canonical 25-invariant mapping for Tailered
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: gh-audit-ruflo.md was not in AUD-L6a's evidence set, so that lane mapped its findings against AGENTS.md:17-36 plus the four accepted ADRs instead, and explicitly asked the coordinator to re-map. AUD-L6a also could not determine `getProjectCwd()` semantics — it is defined in @claude-flow/cli-core@3.7.0-alpha.5, a plain dependency that is not bundled — and if an environment variable can redirect Ruflo's project root it would materially soften the read-only-mount blocker.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: Re-map AUD-L6a's twelve findings against the master specification's canonical invariant list, and resolve getProjectCwd() by reading the installed cli-core package.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Ruflo's non-packaged surfaces — 37 of 38 plugins, v3/plugins/, the 6 Rust crates, and the verification/ evidence set
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: They are absent from the installed artifact (RUF-L2a-002, RUF-L1a-04) and were not assessed for compatibility. No Rust toolchain exists on the audit host, so no crate test could run.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: A separate assessment scoped to the GitHub repository rather than the registry artifact, on a host with cargo installed. Note that anything found there is not what `npm i ruflo` delivers.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Whether ruflo@3.37.0 carries npm provenance / OIDC attestation
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: Requires `npm audit signatures` against the live registry, which was not run. The 3.34.0 changelog claims a Trusted Publishing workflow.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: npm audit signatures against the registry. It would not alter RUF-011, which concerns the vendor's own witness mechanism rather than registry attestation.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

unresolved_areas.area: Shared-evidence integrity note raised by AUD-L5
unresolved_areas.why_blocked: work/install-default grew from 50,012 to 50,016 files during the audit — a 4-file HuggingFace model cache with mtime 15:43. All AUD-L5 mounts of that tree were read-only and its own measurements bracket the change, so AUD-L5's numbers are unaffected. AUD-L5 INFERRED that a concurrent lane mounted install-default writable. It is itself an instance of RUF-507/RUF-313.
unresolved_areas.what_would_resolve_it: Per-lane private install trees, or a read-only enforcement check on shared evidence. Recorded so the file-count discrepancy is not later read as a measurement error.
unresolved_areas.label: UNKNOWN

environment_limitations: linux/arm64 (Apple Silicon) only — no linux/x86_64, no Windows, no native-Linux host
~34 GB free disk against a 1.5 GiB default install footprint
all container filesystem I/O over Docker Desktop macOS virtiofs, which inflates cold-start figures
no pty allocatable from the harness (blocks the interactive `policy budget set` path)
paid model calls forbidden by charter; provider behaviour observed only via fixtures or static reading is labelled INFERRED
network egress sinkholed by default (local DNS + TLS-SNI sinkhole); the only real egress was `npm audit --package-lock-only` to registry.npmjs.org
no writes to main, no merges, no ADR rewrites, no synthetic rows in canonical Tailered ledgers
AUD-L7 integration-spike lanes had not produced their artifacts when this findings set was assembled

host_repository_findings.note: Defects this audit found in the HOST repository (tailered-ai @ 6172653e). These are NOT Ruflo defects and are actionable today, independently of the Ruflo verdict.

findings.summary: product/ confinement is a textual prefix test; product/../decisions/ADR-000.md passes it and overwrites an accepted, immutable ADR.
ProcessAgent passes no cwd or env; agents inherit the company repository and every secret in the parent environment.
timeoutMs does not bound invoke(); a descendant holding stdout disarms the abort and the run hangs unboundedly.
usage is agent-asserted and cross-checked by nothing; a lying agent controls the cost ledger.
AgentResponse carries no model or provider identity, so model-identity law is unverifiable at the boundary.
Cancellation kills only the direct child and never escalates past SIGTERM, leaking the descendant tree.
AgentRequest omits the projection; the agent is never told the ceiling it is measured against.
A failed call writes usage.input = projection.maxTokens into the append-only trace as if measured.
{files: []} is a valid, billable codegen success.
Agent stderr is captured but discarded on success; a successful call has no diagnostic channel.
